notes.meaning: Sin and guilt make people fearful, so the wicked run even when no one is chasing them. In contrast, those who live rightly have a clean conscience and trust in God's protection. This gives them courage as steady and fearless as a young lion.

When a nation turns to sin and rebellion, its government becomes unstable, leading to many rival leaders or rapid turnovers in power. But a wise and discerning leader brings stability and keeps order for a long time. Good leadership is God's gift to preserve peace in a society.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars note that the phrase for maintaining order is difficult to translate, and the many rulers may refer to rapid successions of kings, similar to the period of the judges.

notes.meaning: When a needy person gains power and mistreats the poor, he causes utter ruin. He is compared to a driving rainstorm that washes away crops and soil rather than watering them. Those who have known hardship ought to show mercy, but a harsh ruler from humble origins can be the cruelest of all.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Because the poor in Proverbs usually do not have power to oppress, some scholars suggest altering one Hebrew letter to read 'a wicked ruler,' though ancient manuscripts do not support this change.

notes.meaning: People who abandon God's law end up praising and encouraging the wicked. But those who obey God cannot remain silent and instead stand up against evil deeds. Turning away from God's word destroys moral judgment, while holding to it leads people to resist wrongdoing.

Evil people cannot understand true justice because their wicked desires blind their minds. In contrast, those who seek the Lord receive the wisdom they need to discern right from wrong in every situation. Desiring to obey God opens the door to deeper spiritual understanding.

A poor person who lives with honesty and integrity is far better off than a rich person whose life is crooked and deceitful. Wealth cannot make up for a lack of godliness, nor does poverty diminish true character. An upright life brings peace and honor that money can never buy.

A son who obeys God's instruction shows true wisdom and brings joy to his household. On the other hand, a son who runs with reckless, wasteful companions brings public shame upon his father. The friends a young person keeps reveal his character and affect his entire family.

A person who piles up wealth by charging high interest and taking advantage of the poor will not keep it. In God's providence, those ill-gotten riches will eventually pass into the hands of someone who is kind and generous to the needy. God ensures that dishonest wealth does not bring lasting gain.

When someone deliberately refuses to listen to God's law, God finds even that person's prayers detestable. God expects obedience before he listens to requests. Refusing to hear what God says cuts off genuine fellowship with him.

Anyone who schemes to lead an upright person into sin or danger will fall into the very trap he planned for others. Meanwhile, innocent people who trust God are kept safe and receive good blessings from him. God defends the sincere and turns evil back onto the deceiver.

A rich man often flatters himself into thinking he is exceptionally wise simply because he has wealth. Yet a poor man who has true spiritual discernment can see right through the rich man's empty pride. Real wisdom comes from God, not from a large bank account.

When righteous leaders prosper and rule, the entire nation celebrates and experiences great honor and safety. But when wicked people take power, good citizens are forced to hide themselves to escape injustice and harm. Society flourishes only when godliness is protected.

Trying to hide or make excuses for sin never brings true peace or lasting success. Instead, the person who openly admits his wrongdoing and turns away from it will receive God's mercy and forgiveness. True repentance involves both confessing guilt and choosing a new direction.

A person is truly blessed when he lives with constant reverent awe toward God and a healthy dread of sin. But someone who hardens his heart against God's word and warnings will stumble into ruin. A tender conscience protects a person from spiritual disaster.

A wicked ruler over a poor and helpless people is as dangerous and terrifying as a roaring lion or a hungry bear. Instead of protecting his subjects, he preys upon them and strips away what little they have. Helpless people have no defense against a cruel tyrant except God.

A leader who lacks understanding becomes a harsh oppressor because he thinks only of his own power and gain. In contrast, a ruler who despises dishonest profit and avoids greed will enjoy a long and peaceful life. True statesmanship requires wisdom and unselfishness.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars read this verse not merely as a general observation, but as a direct warning addressed to a foolish ruler.

notes.meaning: A person guilty of murder is tormented by guilt and flees toward the grave, finding no rest. No one should shelter him or help him escape the just punishment for taking a human life. Justice must take its course to honor the value of human life.

The person who walks with integrity and honesty is protected by God and kept safe in difficult times. But the double-dealer who walks in crooked paths will suddenly fall into ruin without any warning. Sincerity gives security, while dishonesty leads to a swift downfall.

The person who works his land faithfully will have plenty of food for his family. But someone who chases after daydreams and keeps company with worthless people will end up filled with poverty. Diligent, honest labor is the reliable way to provide for daily needs.

A faithful, trustworthy person who deals honestly with God and others will receive many blessings. But anyone obsessed with getting rich quickly will easily slip into dishonest schemes and face punishment. Steadiness and faithfulness bring far greater reward than greedy shortcuts.

Showing favoritism in judgment is completely wrong because it perverts fairness. Once a judge or leader compromises his integrity, even a tiny bribe like a crust of bread will persuade him to commit injustice. Partiality quickly ruins a person's conscience.

A stingy and envious man rushes headlong to pile up wealth, thinking only of what he wants. He fails to realize that God's providence will bring sudden poverty upon him. Greed blinds people to the destruction that awaits those who live only for gain.

Someone who offers an honest, constructive correction may hurt at first, but in the long run he will be appreciated. A smooth flatterer may please for a moment, but his words do no real good. True friendship requires the courage to speak the truth in love.

A person who steals from his own parents and claims it is not a sin is just as wicked as a violent criminal. Taking family property or running up debts for parents to pay is a gross breach of love and duty. Treating parents with disrespect and theft is an outrage against God.

A greedy, proud person is never satisfied and constantly causes arguments and division around him. But the one who puts his trust in the Lord enjoys peace of mind and true prosperity. Resting in God's care frees us from the anxious grasping of pride.

Anyone who relies solely on his own feelings, instincts, and ideas is acting like a fool, because the human heart is easily deceived. But the person who walks in the wisdom of God's word will be guided safely through trouble. True safety comes from trusting God rather than self.

Whoever shares generously with the poor will never run short of what he needs, for God rewards openhanded charity. But whoever turns a blind eye to human misery will be loaded with curses from both people and God. Generosity brings God's blessing, while cold indifference brings loss.

When evil people rise to positions of authority, good citizens are forced to retreat into private life for safety. But when wicked rulers fall and perish, righteous people emerge and multiply in the land. Good government allows righteous living to flourish openly.
